newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower led by funds.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower led by funds.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Friday, as chart-based speculative trading strategies by commodity funds accelerated the decline of the past three weeks, traders said.

Investors had little incentive to buy gold while U.S. inflation remained low, the Fed was poised to move pre-emptively to tighten monetary policy, and the U.S. sharemarket and bond market remained healthy, analysts said.
In the bullion market, spot silver slipped to an 18-month low while spot gold and platinum posted fresh two-month lows and palladium set a three-year low.
"There is some concern Russia is having difficulty meeting its budget and may need to sell more commodities to raise revenue," Everen Securities analyst Todd Henrichs said.

"And there's been uncertainty recently about the IMF's plan to sell gold, even though that's been known for some time, but the impetus today came from fund selling after silver fell through the key $5.00 level yesterday," he said.
COMEX December silver ended down 7.7 cents at $4.863 an ounce,m up from a three-year low of $4.840. In the bullion market, silver saw an 18 month low around $4.810 intraday Friday.

But analysts see little change in silver's fundamentals, with another large shortfall between world supply and demand likely this year, though soft seasonal physical demand is currently weighing on the market.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.70 an ounce at $383.90, after falling to a three year low for the December contract at $383.30 intraday.

In the bullion market, spot gold saw a two month low at $380.30, before ending quoted around $380.85/381.35, compared to the London afternoon fix Friday of $381.75 and the New York close Thursday at $382.50/383.00.

Both gold and silver are now near the bottom of ranges that have provided value in the past two or three years, analysts noted, and standard nine-day relative strength indicators (RSI) for December gold and December silver closed in oversold zones at 18.43 percent and 18.59 percent respectively.
"But while these markets remain weak jewellers and other fabricators are likely to buy only what they need," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.

NYMEX October platinum ended down $2.20 at $388.30 an ounce, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $387.60. Spot platinum slipped to a low of $385.10 an ounce, not far from the low of $385.00 seen on July 8.
NYMEX December palladium ended down 95 cents at $120.80, after also seeing a new lows for the December contract at $120.50. Spot market palladium saw fresh three year lows around $118.50 an ounce.

Slow demand from the Japanese electronics industry, concerns over weakening offtake by the auto sectors in the U.S. and Europe and expectations of more Russian supply pressure are depressing the platinum metals group, analysts said. -Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
